title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The Decision of the AI Office outlines the office’s stance on artificial intelligence regulation and governance. It highlights key policy priorities and guidelines for responsible AI development and use.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy announces a vacancy for Technology Specialists in AI at the AI Office, detailing the roles and responsibilities these specialists will hold. It also outlines the qualifications needed, the application process, and how these specialists will support and advance the office’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces a vacancy for a Lead Scientific Adviser in an AI office, inviting qualified candidates to apply. The role involves guiding AI research, shaping strategy, and ensuring ethical and responsible AI development.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy outlines the responsibilities and qualifications required for the position of AI Office Legal Officer. It also details the selection process and expectations for handling legal matters related to AI.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy explains how to manage open positions for AI policy officers. It outlines the responsibilities, selection process, and expected qualifications for filling these roles.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts that reviews the European Union’s proposed AI regulations, evaluating technical feasibility, safety, and ethical implications of AI systems. Their recommendations help lawmakers refine the AI Act to balance innovation with risk mitigation and protect public trust.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document outlines a proposal to create and adopt standardized guidelines for the development and deployment of AI systems. It calls for collaboration among industry, academia, and regulators to define, implement, and monitor these standards to ensure safety, transparency, and compliance.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The notice announces a public consultation on creating or updating a Community of Practice related to AI. It invites stakeholders to share their views on the group's purpose, structure, and how it will support responsible AI use.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The document announces a call for people to express interest in joining a new Community of Practice. It invites individuals or organizations to apply if they want to collaborate on shared learning and development within the field.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document explains how a Community of Practice (CoP) creates and refines documents through an iterative drafting process, showing the stages from initial draft to final version. It highlights the key steps—drafting, reviewing, gathering feedback, revising, and repeating these cycles—to improve quality and collaboration.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document is a visual timeline that charts the stages of drafting the AI policy, starting from initial discussions, through drafting drafts, reviewing feedback, and finalizing the policy. It highlights key dates and milestones to show how the policy evolved from conception to completion.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document presents the first draft of a code of practice for AI, outlining key principles for responsible development and deployment. It emphasizes transparency, fairness, accountability, and safety to guide organizations in implementing AI responsibly.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document presents the second draft of a Code of Practice, offering revised guidelines for responsible AI development and deployment. It emphasizes principles such as transparency, accountability, fairness, and privacy to help organizations align their AI activities with ethical and regulatory expectations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The document outlines a set of guidelines for best practices in AI development and deployment. As the third draft, it builds on previous iterations to refine principles, responsibilities, and compliance measures for stakeholders.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for governments, businesses, and civil society to set shared rules and best practices around artificial intelligence. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, safety, and the protection of human rights as guiding principles for AI development and deployment.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a comprehensive agreement that establishes shared rules for the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It outlines principles such as safety, transparency, accountability, and the protection of human rights while encouraging international cooperation and the exchange of best practices.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines set out the specific artificial‑intelligence activities that are forbidden, such as creating harmful deepfakes, weaponizing AI, or manipulating people’s opinions without transparency. They explain why these practices are disallowed and outline the potential legal and ethical repercussions for those who violate them.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document sets out clear criteria for what should be considered an AI system, helping organizations identify and classify AI technologies. It also explains the responsibilities and compliance requirements that follow from those definitions to promote consistent and transparent AI governance.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: The policy outlines how the government plans to communicate and support initiatives that boost start‑up growth and spur innovation, especially through technology and AI. It focuses on outreach, collaboration, and resource sharing to create a more vibrant and competitive entrepreneurial ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start‑Ups is a European program that provides early‑stage companies with access to high‑performance computing resources to accelerate their research and product development. It offers powerful computing clusters, technical support, and training to help start‑ups innovate, scale, and compete in advanced technology markets.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy outlines a webinar designed to educate participants about managing risks associated with artificial intelligence systems. It provides guidance on identifying potential hazards, implementing safeguards, and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations during AI development and deployment.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The document is a video webinar titled “Risk Management” that explains how to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks in various settings. It offers practical tools and strategies for organizations to create and implement effective risk‑management plans.
